name: Minneapolis–Saint Paul International Airport / Wold–Chamberlain Field
before:
The main gateway to the Twin Cities sits on 2,930 acres of land that belongs to no city at all, an unorganized territory wedged against the boundaries of Minneapolis and Richfield. Despite that oddity, it is about as central as an airport gets, within 10 miles of both downtown Minneapolis and downtown Saint Paul, which makes the transfer into either city short by American standards.

Most passengers arriving here are flying Delta or one of its regional partners, which between them account for roughly 65% of traffic. It is one of Delta's major hubs, so connections are plentiful and the terminals are busy with people changing planes rather than ending their journey. Sun Country and Endeavor Air, both Minnesota outfits, also call it home.

There is a military side too. The airport shares its runways with an Air Reserve Station supporting Air Force Reserve Command and Air National Guard operations, including the 934th Airlift Wing, so the occasional military aircraft is part of the scenery. Cargo operators use it heavily as well. The Metropolitan Airports Commission runs the whole thing, along with six smaller regional airfields.
after:
The main airport for the Twin Cities sits on 2,930 acres that belong to no city at all, though it borders Minneapolis and Richfield. It is about seven miles south of downtown Minneapolis.

Most passengers here fly Delta or one of its regional partners, and MSP is one of Delta's major hubs. Sun Country and Endeavor Air also call it home.

There is a military side too. The airport shares its runways with an Air Reserve Station, home to the 934th Airlift Wing. Cargo airlines use it as well. The Metropolitan Airports Commission runs the airport, along with six smaller airfields in the region.

claims.inAfter: The main airport for the Twin Cities
claims.note: Was 'The main gateway to the Twin Cities': 'gateway to' is a banned phrase. The other airports the operator runs are general aviation fields (see the last claim); the FAA's table puts MSP 17th in the US with 17.5 million boardings in 2025. mspairport.com is OurAirports' home link for KMSP.

claims.claim: about as central as an airport gets; within 10 miles of downtown Saint Paul; short transfer
claims.wasBefore: Despite that oddity, it is about as central as an airport gets, within 10 miles of both downtown Minneapolis and downtown Saint Paul, which makes the transfer into either city short by American standards.
claims.why: The Saint Paul distance rests on Wikipedia alone, and 'as central as an airport gets' and 'short by American standards' are unsourced judgements. The Minneapolis distance is kept, made specific (about seven miles).

claims.why: The sources differ: Wikipedia 65 per cent, the operator's 2025 Annual Report 70 per cent; BTS's carrier-share page could not be reached (404). Softened to 'most' (above).

claims.claim: two terminals not connected airside
claims.why: Held back: verified with two sources, but a new fact that replaces nothing in the old text. The two terminals are about a mile apart, off separate roadways, with no walkway between them: passengers change terminals on the free light rail. Worth adding for agents if Andy agrees: it is the thing most likely to catch a traveller out. Was to read: 'There are two terminals, off separate roads and not connected on foot: check which one your airline uses, and allow for the free light rail between them.'
